methodology: The original research topic and the generated technical specification were decomposed into atomic information units based on individual requirements, features, behaviors, and constraints. Each atomic unit is designed to be independent, self-contained, technically specific, unambiguous, and implementable as a single requirement. This decomposition facilitates a detailed comparison to assess the coverage and similarity between the original topic and the generated specification.
mindtraced_atomic_units: The shift register also functions as a down counter
Data is shifted in MSB first when shift_ena is 1
The number in the shift register is decremented when count_ena is 1
Behavior is undefined when both shift_ena and count_ena are 1
Shift operation takes priority when both shift_ena and count_ena are 1
spec_atomic_units: Module has a clock input clk
Module has shift enable input shift_ena
Module has count enable input count_ena
Module has a data input data
Module has a 4-bit output register q
Combinational logic determines the next value of register q based on inputs shift_ena, count_ena, data, and current value of q
If shift_ena = 1 and count_ena = 0, q_next[3:0] = {data, q[3:1]}
If shift_ena = 0 and count_ena = 1, q_next[3:0] = q[3:0] - 1
If shift_ena = 0 and count_ena = 0, q_next[3:0] = q[3:0]
If shift_ena = 1 and count_ena = 1, q_next[3:0] = {data, q[3:1]}
Shift operation has priority when both enables are asserted
The register's value changes on the positive edge of the clock clk
When shift_ena is high, q shifts in data
When count_ena is high and shift_ena is low, q decrements
